source.request: a website for my small bakery

answers.question: What should it have?
answers.answer: Our cakes and prices, opening hours, where we are, a contact page

title: A website for your bakery
summary: You'll build a small two-page website for your bakery: a home page with your cakes, prices, opening hours and address, plus a contact page.
outcome: A friendly bakery website that works offline from your folder, with a menu to move between the home page and the contact page.

simpler.title: Just the home page with your cakes
simpler.why: Get one lovely page showing off your cakes and opening hours first; you can add the contact page and extra styling later.

steps.title: Start the page
steps.instruction: Create a file called index.html. At the very top, type the start of every web page: the line <!DOCTYPE html>, then an html part that holds a head part and a body part.
steps.why: Every web page needs this frame: the head holds info about the page, the body holds what people see.

checks.say: I can't find your index.html file yet.
Something in your page frame looks unfinished. Check every part you opened is closed.

hints: A web page starts with a line saying it is a web page, then one big part that holds two smaller parts: one for info, one for what you see.
Type <!DOCTYPE html> first, then <html>. Inside it put <head></head> and then <body></body>, each on their own lines, and finish with </html>.

<!DOCTYPE …>
<html>
<head>
</…>
…
</html>

concept.title: The page frame
concept.explain: html wraps the whole page, head holds hidden info about it, and body holds everything people see.
concept.imageQuery: basic html page structure head body diagram

steps.title: Give the page a name
steps.instruction: Inside the head, add three lines: a meta line with charset set to utf-8, a title saying Sweet Crumbs Bakery, and a link to a style file called style.css (rel="stylesheet" href="style.css").
steps.why: meta lets emojis show properly, title names the browser tab, and link connects the style file you'll write later.

checks.say: I can't see the name of your page for the browser tab yet.
Add the line that tells the browser which letters to use (utf-8).
Your page isn't connected to the style file style.css yet.
checks.name: href

hints: The head holds information about the page: which letters it uses, its tab name, and where its style lives.
Between <head> and </head> add a <meta> with charset="utf-8", a <title> with your bakery name, and a <link> with rel="stylesheet" and href="style.css".

<meta charset="…">
<title>…</title>
<link rel="…" href="…">

concept.title: Page info in the head
concept.explain: The head tells the browser the page's name, its letters, and which style file to use.

steps.title: Add a footer
steps.instruction: Inside the body, add a footer. In the footer, put a paragraph saying Fresh baked every morning.
steps.why: A footer is the strip at the bottom of a page; a paragraph (p) holds a line of normal text.

checks.say: I can't see the bottom strip of your page yet.

concept.title: Footers and paragraphs
concept.explain: A footer is the bottom strip of a page, and p is a normal paragraph of text.

steps.title: Add the header and menu
steps.instruction: Right under the opening body line (above the footer), add a header. In it put a big heading (h1) saying 🧁 Sweet Crumbs Bakery, then a paragraph with two links: Home going to index.html, and Contact going to contact.html, with a | between them.
steps.why: The header is the top of your page, h1 is the biggest heading, and a makes a link you can click.

checks.say: I can't see your big heading at the top yet.
I can't see a link to your Contact page yet.
I can't see a link back to your Home page yet.

hints: The top of the page needs your bakery's name in big letters and a small menu with two links.

concept.title: Headers, headings and links
concept.explain: header is the top area, h1 is the biggest title, and a turns words into a link to another page.

steps.title: Start the cakes section
steps.instruction: Under the header, add a section. Inside it, put a smaller heading (h2) saying Our Cakes.
steps.why: A section groups one topic of your page, and h2 is a heading one size smaller than h1.

checks.say: I can't see a part of your page with the heading Our Cakes yet.

hints: Make a new part of the page for your cakes, with its own title.
After </header>, open <section>, put an <h2> inside with the words Our Cakes, then close </section>.

concept.title: Sections
concept.explain: A section is a box that holds one topic of your page, like your cakes.

steps.title: List your cakes
steps.instruction: Under the Our Cakes heading, add a bullet list (ul) with 4 items (li): 🍰 Strawberry cake - £3.50 a slice, 🎂 Chocolate cake - £3.00 a slice, 🥕 Carrot cake - £3.20 a slice, and 🧁 Cupcake - £2.00 each.
steps.why: ul makes a bullet list and each li is one bullet, perfect for a menu with prices.
steps.expected:
• 🍰 Strawberry cake - £3.50 a slice
  • 🎂 Chocolate cake - £3.00 a slice
  • 🥕 Carrot cake - £3.20 a slice
  • 🧁 Cupcake - £2.00 each

checks.say: I can't see your list of cakes yet.
Your cake list should include the cupcake.

concept.title: Bullet lists
concept.explain: ul starts a bullet list and every li inside it is one bullet point.

steps.title: Add opening hours
steps.instruction: Below the cakes section, add a new section with an h2 saying Opening Hours and a bullet list of 3 items: Monday to Friday: 8am - 5pm, Saturday: 9am - 4pm, Sunday: closed.
steps.why: Customers need to know when they can visit, and you already know every tag you need.

checks.say: I can't see a second part with your opening hours yet.
Your opening hours should mention Sunday.

hints: This is just like your cakes part: a new box with a title and a list.
After the </section> that closes the cakes, open a new <section> with an <h2>, then a <ul> with three <li> lines, and close it all.

steps.instruction: Below the opening hours section, add one more section with an h2 saying Where We Are and two paragraphs: 📍 12 High Street, Townsville and Next to the post office, with a blue door.
steps.why: Now people can find your bakery.

Where We Are

📍 12 High Street, Townsville

Next to the post office, with a blue door.

checks.say: I can't see a third part with your address yet.
Your address part should have the heading Where We Are.

steps.title: Look at your home page
steps.instruction: Open index.html in your web browser (double-click it in your folder). You should see your heading, menu, cakes, hours, address and footer. It looks plain for now; colour comes later.
steps.why: Seeing your page in a real browser shows your code works.
hints: Find index.html in your project folder.
Double-click it, or drag it into an open browser window.
If it opens in a text editor, right-click it and choose Open with, then your browser.

quiz.question: Which tag makes one bullet in a list?
quiz.explain: li is one list item; ul is the whole list around them.

steps.title: Start the contact page
steps.instruction: Create a new file called contact.html. Type the same frame as your home page: the DOCTYPE line, html, a head with meta charset utf-8, a title saying Contact - Sweet Crumbs Bakery, the link to style.css, and an empty body.
steps.why: Each page of a website is its own file with its own frame.
steps.expected:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <title>Contact - Sweet Crumbs Bakery</title>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">
</head>
<body>
</body>
</html>

checks.say: I can't find your contact.html file yet.
Your contact page needs a name for the browser tab.
Connect your contact page to the style file style.css too.

hints: Look at the top of index.html: your new page starts almost the same way.
Copy the structure: <!DOCTYPE html>, <html>, <head> with <meta>, <title> and <link>, then <body></body> and </html>. Change the title to Contact - Sweet Crumbs Bakery.

<html>
<head>

  <title>…</title>

steps.title: Same header on every page
steps.instruction: Inside the body of contact.html, add the same header as on your home page: the h1 with 🧁 Sweet Crumbs Bakery and the paragraph with the Home and Contact links.
steps.why: Keeping the same header on every page lets visitors move around easily.

checks.say: I can't see the big heading on your contact page yet.

steps.title: Try your links
steps.instruction: Open index.html in your browser again and click Contact. Your contact page should open. Then click Home to go back.
steps.why: Your two pages are now joined into a real little website.
hints: Open index.html in your browser.
Click the word Contact in the menu at the top.
If it doesn't open, check the link's file name matches contact.html exactly.

quiz.question: What does href="contact.html" in a link do?
options: Says which page opens when you click
quiz.explain: href is the address the link takes you to.

steps.title: Pick a font and background
steps.instruction: Create a new file called style.css. Write a rule for body with two settings: font-family: Georgia, serif; and background: #fff5e6;
steps.why: font-family picks the letter style, and background colours the whole page a warm cream.

checks.say: Your page background isn't cream yet.
I can't find your style.css file yet.
Something in your style file is unfinished. Check the curly brackets and the semicolons.

hints: Style rules start with what you want to change, then the settings inside curly brackets.
Type body, then {. Inside add font-family with Georgia, serif and background with #fff5e6, each ending with ;. Close with }.

concept.title: Style rules
concept.explain: A style rule names a part of the page, then lists settings like colour and font inside curly brackets.

steps.title: Text colour and edges
steps.instruction: Inside the body rule, under the background line, add color: #4a2c1a; and margin: 0;
steps.why: color sets the text colour (a chocolate brown), and margin is the space around the outside of a box; 0 removes the white gap at the page edges.

checks.say: Your text isn't chocolate brown yet.
There's still a gap around the edges of your page.

hints: Add two more settings to the same body rule: one for the text colour, one for the space around the page.
Under the background line, add color with #4a2c1a and margin with 0, each ending with ;.

color: …;
  margin: …;

concept.title: Colour and margin
concept.explain: color changes the text colour, and margin is the empty space outside a box.

steps.title: A pink header
steps.instruction: Below the body rule (leave an empty line), add a rule for header with background: #f4a6b8;, text-align: center; and padding: 20px;
steps.why: text-align: center puts the words in the middle, and padding is the space inside the box around the words.

checks.say: Your header isn't pink yet.
The words in your header aren't in the middle yet.
Give your header some space inside around the words.

hints: Make the top of your page pink, with its words in the middle and some room around them.
Write header { … } with background #f4a6b8, text-align center and padding 20px.

concept.title: Centring and padding
concept.explain: text-align: center puts words in the middle, and padding adds space inside a box around its words.
concept.imageQuery: css box model padding margin diagram

steps.title: Style the menu links
steps.instruction: Below the header rule, add a rule for a (the links) with color: #4a2c1a; and font-size: 18px;
steps.why: font-size sets how big the letters are; brown links match your page instead of plain blue.

checks.say: Your menu links aren't a bit bigger yet.
Your menu links are still blue; make them brown.

hints: Links are blue by default; give them your brown colour and slightly bigger letters.
Write a rule for a with color #4a2c1a and font-size 18px.

concept.title: Text size
concept.explain: font-size sets how big the letters are, measured in px (tiny screen dots).

steps.title: Turn sections into cards
steps.instruction: Below the a rule, add a rule for section with background: white;, margin: 20px;, padding: 20px;, border: 2px solid #f4a6b8; and border-radius: 12px;
steps.why: border draws a line around the box, and border-radius rounds its corners, so each section looks like a little card.

checks.say: Your sections don't have a white background yet.
Round the corners of your sections.
Add space around the outside of your sections.
Your sections don't have a solid line around them yet.
The line around your sections should be pink (#f4a6b8).
Add space inside your sections.

hints: Make each section a white card with space around it, space inside it, a pink edge and round corners.
Write section { … } with background white, margin 20px, padding 20px, border 2px solid #f4a6b8 and border-radius 12px.

concept.title: Borders and round corners
concept.explain: border draws a line around a box, and border-radius makes its corners round.

steps.title: Colour the headings
steps.instruction: Below the section rule, add a rule for h2 with color: #c0506b; (a raspberry pink).
steps.why: Coloured headings make each card's title stand out.

checks.say: Your section headings aren't raspberry pink yet.

hints: Give the titles of your cards their own colour.
Write a rule for h2 with color set to #c0506b.

steps.title: Tidy the footer
steps.instruction: Below the h2 rule, add a rule for footer with text-align: center; and padding: 10px;
steps.why: A centred footer with some space finishes the page neatly.

checks.say: The words in your footer aren't in the middle yet.
Give your footer a little space inside.

hints: Centre the bottom line just like you did the header, with a bit less space.
Write a rule for footer with text-align center and padding 10px.

steps.title: Admire your bakery website
steps.instruction: Refresh index.html in your browser. You should see a pink header, white cards with round corners and raspberry headings. Click Contact to check that page is styled too.
steps.why: One style file dresses up both pages at once.
hints: Go back to the browser tab with your page.
Press the refresh button or F5.
If nothing changed, check both pages link to style.css.

quiz.question: What does padding do?
options: Adds space inside a box around its words
quiz.explain: Padding is the space inside the box; margin is the space outside it.
